label: baseline: pattern engine only, no Claude recordings yet

errors.rationale: 'Will be sent ... once she has established care' is a future intention, not evidence of transmission (future tense, so unclear is also acceptable).
The summary's boilerplate says 'Provider list given per protocol' but the case manager states the facility list was not reviewed with the daughter: contradictory at best.
There is no author signature. A compliance 'QA attestation' and the phrase 'Signature on file' are not the physician authenticating the summary.
The summary is unsigned and only 14 days have passed since discharge on 2026-11-13, so it is still inside the 30-day window.
Blood culture final and Legionella antigen were outstanding; the only 'None pending' statement sits under template text marked Do Not Use, which also contradicts the hospital course.
The HIM note says the summary was not yet transmitted; the 'sent electronically' sentence is unused template text.
The real note says the patient declined to discuss plans and the team would revisit; no later discussion is documented. The 'verbalized understanding' line is template text.
No freedom-of-choice discussion is documented; the phrase 'freedom of choice' appears only in the request to mark it N/A.
No quality data was shared; the words 'quality data' appear only in the N/A request.
No PCP or follow-up clinician is named anywhere in the bundle; the orthopedic appointment names only a clinic, and the DocumentReference author is metadata the flattened text does not contain.
The only 'Goals of Care' text is a Goal resource addressed to the reviewer; there is no code status, advance directive or patient goal.

The narrative states the patient and wife were not offered a list; the contrary claim lives only in a scheduling Appointment description. Contradictory, and the narrative is the clinical documentation.
The narrative says the unit placed the referral to the affiliated agency and the family would have preferred another; choice was not respected.
The narrative says no quality information was given; the Care Compare claim appears only in the Appointment description.
The visible note says there is no PCP and names only a clinic for follow-up; 'Dr. Nadia Fields' appears only inside a hidden HTML comment that contradicts it.
The note says the summary will be routed later; the 'faxed to PCP' claim is inside the HTML comment and contradicted.
Case management note documents that a list of Medicare-certified providers of the referred level of care was given to the patient and family.
Listed under 'Diagnoses at discharge, in order of importance' rather than a templated header.
'How he is at discharge: good condition' with vitals, mental status (alert and oriented) and walking unaided.
'He goes home to his apartment. He doesn't need home services.'
Prose paragraph names started, stopped (ibuprofen), held (losartan) and unchanged medications with reasons.
Biopsies including H. pylori staining are outstanding and Dr. Nakamura's GI office is named to follow them up.
Case manager's assessment of post-discharge needs, supports and medication access is described in prose.
Plan was gone over with the patient and his sister, who explained it back and agrees.
Both lists contain pantoprazole, amlodipine, ferrous sulfate and acetaminophen; losartan is held and absent from both.
Narrative under 'Why she was here and what happened' describes treatment and recovery.
'Her state today: stable and back to herself' with mental status and mobility.
'Where she is going: Fairhaven Gardens, a skilled nursing facility (SNF)'.
'Results not yet back: none. All cultures are final.'
Plan explained to the patient and daughter, who agreed (summary and CM note).
Case manager printed every Medicare-certified SNF within 10 miles (seven) and walked the patient and daughter through it.
Note says the decision is theirs, any facility on the sheet, and the facility they chose was used.
EDGE (terse): 'Dx: acute alcoholic pancreatitis' states the final diagnosis even without a formal section header.
EDGE (terse): 'Condition: stable, A&O x3, ... ambulatory' gives clinical and mental status at discharge.
No PCP or follow-up clinician is named.
Thiamine and folic acid are listed with dose, route and frequency as the discharge medications.
Risks of leaving, return precautions and the plan were discussed with the patient, who agreed (written as 'w/ pt').
LTCH is a post-acute referral; the Medicare-participating LTCH list is documented.
The section only points to a portal list; the summary itself contains no medication list (the changes list covers three drugs, not the full regimen).
A test and a timeframe are given, but no clinician or clinic the patient should see.
TSH and A1c are listed as pending, but no one is named to follow them up.
The Primary Care Provider header is empty and the only follow-up is with a clinic, not a named clinician.
The Goals of Care header is empty; there is no code status or stated treatment preference.
The summary defers the medication list to a separate transfer MAR that was not provided; only changes are listed.
The discharge diagnoses are listed under 'Impression at Discharge', a common synonym the section list does not include; the content is complete.
Follow-up is in a 'Plan' paragraph: PMD Dr. Ostrowski in 1 wk and pulmonary clinic with Dr. Wielicki in 4-6 wks; who and when are both stated.
The primary care clinician is named as 'her PMD, Dr. Nadia Ostrowski' with a phone number; PMD is a standard synonym for PCP.
A full dosed discharge medication list appears under the abbreviated header 'Meds at d/c'.
'Dispo: home w/ wife, no services needed' states the disposition in standard shorthand.
'Outstanding at d/c' lists blood cultures (no growth at 48h, final pending) and names PCP Dr. Lindqvist to follow them up, which is what the rule asks for.
'Resus status: full resuscitation' is the code status, and the patient's stated goal and advance directive preference are recorded.
'Plan reviewed w/ pt + wife at bedside; both agreeable' and the nursing teach-back show the plan was discussed with the patient and his wife.
The only mentions of discussing the plan are unchecked template boxes in the CM note and the nursing education checklist; an unchecked box documents nothing.
'List of Medicare-certified home health agencies ... provided' is an unchecked box; nothing shows a list was given.
The freedom-of-choice box is unchecked and 'Agency selected by patient' is blank; a referral to one agency does not show the patient chose it.
The Care Compare quality-data box is unchecked.
'Discharge Condition: See progress note' points to a document that was not provided and the summary itself never states the condition at discharge.
'See above' refers back to the hospital course, which mentions gastric biopsies for H. pylori but never says whether they are pending or who will follow them up.
'Goals of Care: Per CM' defers to the case management note, which contains no code status, advance directive or stated goals.
The pending urine culture is listed, but the note says 'No one has been assigned to follow up on the result', so the follow-up owner the rule requires is missing.
The section only records that the proxy 'declined to discuss' and that the topic was 'never addressed'; no code status, directive or goals are documented.
The fax was rejected and the note says 'Never transmitted'; an attempted send is not evidence the summary reached the PCP.

The patient lacks capacity and the CM note says the plan was 'to be reviewed' with the daughter but 'no one available'; nursing confirms no teach-back, so no discussion with the patient or representative is documented.
'Will likely need cardiology follow-up in 2-3 weeks' is a hedge, nothing is scheduled, and the nursing note only says to call 'if palpitations continue'; no committed who-and-when.
The pending TSH is listed, but 'plan to have someone from the team follow up' names no responsible clinician.
'To be faxed ... once signed' is future tense; there is no evidence the summary was actually sent.
The section says the evaluation 'will be completed' by case management; no CM note was provided and no evaluation content is written.
'None pending' contradicts the hospital course, which says blood cultures from 11/15 'remain in process at the time of discharge', and no one is named to follow them.
The summary says DNR/DNI (confirmed 11/11) but the later CM note records the patient now wants full code and asked for the order to be updated; the record contradicts itself on code status.
The summary's 'Principal Diagnosis' section only says 'Refer to case management note'; the diagnosis appears only in the CM note, which this rule does not accept.
'Discharge Medications: As per nursing discharge instructions' is a cross-reference, not a list; the list exists only in the nursing document, which this rule does not accept.
'PCP: None' states there is no PCP, and follow-up is with a clinic, not a named clinician.
'cc: None' says the summary was copied to no one, and nothing else shows it was sent to the clinic.

The only signature line belongs to the H&P copied into the summary (Dr. Okonjo, 2026-11-08, before discharge); the attending signature line is blank and marked pending, so the summary itself is unsigned.
The summary is unsigned and only 15 days have passed since discharge on 2026-11-12, so it is still inside the 30-day window.
The summary was faxed to Brightwater Home Health, which is no longer the receiving provider; nothing shows it was sent to Lakeview or the PCP.
The provider list documented in the CM note was of home health agencies for the superseded plan; no list of SNFs was presented for the actual SNF referral.
Freedom of choice and the patient's selection are documented only for the home health agency; nothing shows she chose Lakeview or was offered a choice of SNFs.
Care Compare ratings were reviewed for home health agencies only, not for SNFs.
'Went over the plan with both of them ... They are on board' documents a discussion with the patient and her sister and their agreement.
'I gave them the county roster of Medicare-certified nursing homes that have rehab beds (14 facilities)' is the Medicare-participating provider list, phrased as a roster.
The CM told her 'the decision is hers alone', offered referrals anywhere she wanted, and her first choice (Harbor View) is the facility she went to.
'We went through the CMS five-star scores and the staffing and inspection results for each facility' is quality data shared to support the choice.

The summary names Dr. Priya Raman (nephrology) and a lab before the visit but no date; the nursing instructions give the confirmed appointment with Dr. Raman on Tuesday, December 1 at 10:30 AM. Both are accepted documents, so who and when are documented.
The 'What's different from before' list says lisinopril is off, furosemide went from 40 to 20 mg, bicarbonate was added and amlodipine went up, each with a reason.
'Outstanding at discharge' lists the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and says Dr. Raman's office will follow it up.
The nursing section 'Getting around at home' describes rollator use, standby help for showering and stair ability; the summary adds 'Up and walking on the unit'.
